How to read this summary
Deductible. The amount you pay for covered services before the plan begins to pay.
Copay. A fixed dollar amount you pay for a covered service, usually when you get the service.
Coinsurance. Your share of the cost of a covered service, calculated as a percent of the allowed
amount.
Allowed amount. The maximum amount the plan considers for a covered service from a network
provider.
Out-of-pocket limit. The most you pay in a year for covered services. Once you reach it, the plan pays
100% of covered services.
Network provider. A provider that has a contract with the plan. You usually pay less in network.

How your plan works
Advavate Select PPO gives you a network of doctors, hospitals and other providers. You can see
providers outside the network, but you usually pay more, and out-of-network providers can bill you for
amounts above the allowed amount.
You do not need a referral to see a specialist. Some services, such as inpatient stays and certain
imaging, need prior authorization. Your provider normally asks for it on your behalf.
When you get care, we pay the provider and send you an Explanation of Benefits. It is not a bill.
Compare it with any bill you receive from the provider.
Emergency care is covered at the in-network level, at any hospital, if you reasonably believe you need
emergency care.

Advavate Health
Gold PPO 25/1000/10%
SYNTHETIC SAMPLE - fictional insurer and plan made for software testing. Not real coverage.
Page 3 of 6
Your costs
Deductible. Your annual deductible is $1,000 for each person in-network and $2,000 for a family.
Out-of-network, the annual deductible is $2,000 per person. You pay the allowed amount for services
subject to the deductible until it is met. Office visits that have a copay are not subject to the deductible.
Out-of-pocket maximum. The most you will pay in a plan year for covered in-network services is
$4,500 per person and $9,000 per family. Out-of-network, the out-of-pocket maximum is $9,000 per
person and $18,000 per family. Your deductible, copays and coinsurance all count toward the maximum.
Premiums, balance-billing charges and services this plan doesn't cover do not.
Once you reach your out-of-pocket maximum, we pay 100% of the allowed amount for covered
in-network services for the rest of the plan year.

Advavate Health
Gold PPO 25/1000/10%

Page 4 of 6
Coinsurance and allowed amounts
After you meet your deductible, you pay 10% of the allowed amount for most covered in-network
services, and Advavate pays 90%. For out-of-network services, you pay 40% of the allowed amount after
the deductible.
Advavate's maximum payment is up to $380 per admission for certain out-of-network freestanding
facilities. You are responsible for any charges above that amount.
The allowed amount is the amount Advavate has agreed to pay a network provider for a service.
Network providers agree to accept the allowed amount as full payment for covered services, apart from
your deductible, copay and coinsurance.

Claims, explanation of benefits and notes
After you get care, we send an Explanation of Benefits (EOB). An EOB is not a bill. It shows what the
provider charged, what the plan allowed, what the plan paid and what you may owe.
If you have other health coverage, we work with the other plan to decide which pays first. This is called
coordination of benefits.
This plan has in-network benefits only, except for emergencies. If you have questions about a claim,
contact member services.
